issues.legal_issue: A second appellate court cannot overturn concurrent findings of fact merely because it considers the admissible and relevant evidence insufficient to support them.
material_facts: The lower trial and first appellate courts both found that the claimants had established title and possession, based on their assessment of oral and documentary evidence.
The second appellate court reassessed that evidence and rejected the concurrent findings, although no question of document construction or legal inference arose.
The Supreme Court found that the second appellate court had exceeded the limits of its factual-review jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The second appellate court had no authority to disturb the concurrent findings on the ground that the evidence was insufficient; its decree was set aside and the first appellate decree was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a second appeal does not permit review of the sufficiency or adequacy of admissible and relevant evidence supporting findings of fact. Admissibility is a question of law, but evidentiary sufficiency is for the courts of fact. A second appeal cannot be entertained merely because a factual finding is erroneous, however gross or inexcusable the error appears. Considerations of equity and fair play cannot enlarge the jurisdiction beyond the express statutory limits. The Court relied on Mussummat Durga Choudhrain v. Jawahir Singh Choudhri (1890), Deity Pattabhiramaswami v. S. Hanymayya (1959), and R. Ramachandra Ayyar v. Ramalingam Chettiar (1963).

rule.if: second_appeal and concurrent_fact_findings and admissible_relevant_evidence and high_court_reassessed_evidence_sufficiency and no_independent_question_of_law

predicates.second_appeal: The challenged proceeding was a second appeal from a lower court's decision.
predicates.concurrent_fact_findings: The trial court and the first appellate court reached the same findings of fact.
predicates.admissible_relevant_evidence: The lower courts relied on evidence that was admissible and relevant to the factual findings.
predicates.high_court_reassessed_evidence_sufficien: The second appellate court reconsidered whether the evidence was sufficient to support the factual findings.
predicates.no_independent_question_of_law: The dispute did not involve a question of document construction or drawing an inference of law.

issues.definition: When a second appeal involves concurrent factual findings based on admissible and relevant evidence, and the second appellate court reconsiders evidentiary sufficiency without an independent question of law, it must not disturb those findings merely for evidentiary insufficiency.
